newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.10 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent a lb lower on Monday based on market orders at 1018 EDT, traders said.

Prices are expected to follow-through on losses made Friday amid technically-driven speculative selling. The benchmark December contract ended down 0.68 cent at 73.35 cents per lb, having ranged from 74.20 to 73.25 cents. The rest of the board finished 0.62 to 0.18 cent lower.
Support in December was seen at 72.00 cents followed by 70.35 cents, the lifetime low of the now-expired July contract.

Players await the U.S. Department of Agriculture's weekly crop condition report released after the close. Analysts said hot dry weather that has blanked much of the U.S. cotton belt for the past several weeks has helped crop development.
Weather Services Corp said bolls are opening in south Texas amid favorable weather conditions, while cotton continues to show good growth and development in California and Arizona.

Tuesday's spec/hedge report should provide the market with its next technical signal, as the speculators are believed to be holding a hefty net short position compared with a 38.2 percent net long position last week, analysts said.
